s: Nicotelea is the mother of Aristomenes (according to the Messenian account of his birth)
q: For they say that a demon or god in the form of a dragon had an intrigue with Nicotelea his mother.

s: Tyrtæus is a schoolmaster (sent from Athens to Sparta)
q: And the Athenians neither wishing that the Lacedæmonians should get the best part of the Peloponnese without great danger, nor to disobey the god, took counsel accordingly, and sent to Sparta one Tyrtæus a schoolmaster, who was thought to have very little intelligence and was lame in one foot.

s: Tyrtæus composes Tyrtæus’s elegiac verses (about the former war)
q: as to Tyrtæus, though he has not mentioned expressly the time, yet one may suppose he has hinted it in the following passage,--in the elegiac lines he wrote about the former war.

s: Lacedæmonians receives recitation from Tyrtæus (privately to the authorities and publicly to all whom he could collect together)
q: And he on his arrival there recited his elegiac verses and his anapæsts privately to the authorities, and publicly to all whom he could collect together.

s: Arcadians allies with Messenians (during the second Messenian War)
q: The Messenians had the men of Elis and Arcadia as their allies in the action, and had moreover help from Argos and Sicyon.

s: Aristodemus reigns for six years and a few months
q: And he died after a reign of six years and a few months.

s: Argives allies with Messenians (during the second Messenian War)
q: The Messenians had the men of Elis and Arcadia as their allies in the action, and had moreover help from Argos and Sicyon.

s: Corinthians allies with Lacedæmonians (during the second Messenian War)
q: And to the help of the Lacedæmonians came the Corinthians, and some of the people of Lepreum from hatred to the men of Elis.

s: Asinæi is neutral in the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians (at the battle at Boar’s Memorial)
q: The Asinæi were neutral.

s: temple of Zeus at Ithome is located at Ithome (within the walls)
q: for as they were in possession of the temple of Zeus within the walls of Ithome, they thought the Lacedæmonians could not be beforehand with them in erecting tripods.

s: Pythian Priestess gives the oracle
q: And this was the oracle the Pythian Priestess gave.

s: Artemis has statue of brass (the statue dropped its shield)
q: For the statue of Artemis, which was of brass as well as the armour, dropped its shield;

s: Athene Poliuchus and Chalciœcus has temple at Sparta (where Aristomenes hung up a shield)
q: Accordingly he went by night to Lacedæmon and hung up a shield at the temple of Athene Chalciœcus, and on it was the inscription, “Aristomenes offers this to the goddess from Spartan spoils.”

s: Damis stays with Aristodemus
q: And he appointed Cleonnis to the command here, and himself and Damis stayed with the light-armed troops, and a few slingers and archers: most in this part of the army were well adapted physically for attack and retreat, and lightly armed.

s: Phyleus assists Damis (as a coadjutor)
q: And he, having selected Cleonnis and Phyleus as his coadjutors, made preparations for the campaign according to his best ability under the circumstances: for he was pressed hard by the siege, and not least by famine and the fear that famine inspired that they could not hold out from want of supplies.

s: Aristomenes is a Messenian leader
q: And this was the disposition of Aristomenes.

s: Theoclus the seer interprets oracle of the Pythian Priestess concerning Messene (as foretelling the imminent end of Messene)
q: And the seer Theoclus having noticed it conjectured that by the he-goat drinking of the Neda the Pythian Priestess meant this wild fig, and that therefore the fate of Messene was imminent.

s: Aristocrates is a king and general of the Arcadians (son of Icetas and native of Trapezus)
q: the Lacedæmonians bribed Aristocrates, the son of Icetas, a native of Trapezus, king and general of the Arcadians at this period.

s: Aristocrates betrays Arcadians (after accepting money from Lacedæmon)
q: And Aristocrates when he had received money from Lacedæmon, at first hid his plans from the Arcadians, but when they were on the eve of an engagement, then he threw them into consternation

s: Messenians takes up residence the mountain Eira (after leaving Andania and other towns in the heart of the country)
q: And Aristomenes after the battle collected the Messenian fugitives, and persuaded them to leave Andania and any other towns in the heart of the country, and to take up their residence on the mountain Eira.

s: Messenians resist at Eira (for eleven years after the disaster at The Great Trench)
q: However they resisted and held out for eleven years after the disaster at _The Great Trench_.

s: Messenians occupy Eira (under siege)
q: And when they assembled there they were besieged by the Lacedæmonians who wished to take them.

s: Messenians raid Laconia (from Eira)
q: And the Messenians when they were hemmed in at Eira, and debarred the rest of their country, except what was occupied by the people of Pylos near the sea, and the people of Mothone, plundered Laconia and their own country

s: Lacedæmonians bribe Aristocrates (before the battle at the Great Trench)
q: the Lacedæmonians bribed Aristocrates, the son of Icetas, a native of Trapezus, king and general of the Arcadians at this period.

s: Aristomenes has in close attendance Eighty picked men of the Messenians (about the same age as himself)
q: Eighty picked men of the Messenians about the same age as himself were in close attendance upon him

s: Lacedæmonians employ Helots (as replacements for dead soldiers)
q: Tyrtæus put heart into them by reciting his verses, and got some Helots enrolled into the regiments in place of the dead men.

s: Arcadians support Messenians (at the battle of the Great Trench)
q: when an engagement was about to take place at what was called _The Great Trench_, and when the Arcadians had come from all their cities to help the Messenians

s: Messene is endangered by some sacred records (if they are lost)
q: The Messenians had some sacred records, which if lost would ruin Messene and keep her under for ever, but which if preserved would, according to the oracular utterances of Lycus the son of Pandion, give the Messenians a chance one day to recover their country

s: Eira is defended by Messenians (during the siege)
q: And when they assembled there they were besieged by the Lacedæmonians who wished to take them. However they resisted and held out for eleven years after the disaster at _The Great Trench_.

s: Ceadas is a underground cavern (used by the Lacedæmonians for condemned malefactors)
q: These were all condemned by the Lacedæmonians to be thrown into their underground cavern called Ceadas; where they throw in their greatest malefactors.

s: siege of Eira lasts eleven years (after the disaster at the Great Trench)
q: However they resisted and held out for eleven years after the disaster at _The Great Trench_. That that was the time the blockade lasted is plain from the verses of Rhianus about the Lacedæmonians.

s: fall of Eira is oracularly foretold to Aristomenes and Theoclus
q: in the 11th year of the siege it was fated that Eira should fall, and that the Messenians should be dispersed, and the god accomplished what had been oracularly foretold to Aristomenes and Theoclus

s: Messenian resistance at Eira lasts eleven years (after the disaster at the Great Trench)
q: However they resisted and held out for eleven years after the disaster at _The Great Trench_.

s: Aristomenes has Aristomenes's shield (a votive offering at Lebadea)
q: And afterwards he took the shield, and hung it up as a votive offering at Lebadea, and I have myself seen it hanging up there. Its design is an eagle with its wings extended at the upper part of the shield.

s: Aristomenes offers Hecatomphonia (after killing one hundred enemies)
q: It was of very remote antiquity, and any Messenian who had killed 100 enemies had a right to offer it. And Aristomenes first offered this sacrifice when he fought the battle at _Boar’s Memorial_, and the slaughter of these Corinthians by night gave him the right to offer this sacrifice a second time.

s: Aristomenes buries sacred records of Messene (on Mount Ithome for the future recovery of Messene)
q: and Aristomenes knowing these oracular utterances conveyed away by night these _arcana_: and going to the most unfrequented part of Mount Ithome buried them there

s: Aristomenes is saved by Messenian maiden (after capture by Cretan bowmen)
q: She therefore poured out wine freely for the Cretans, till drink overpowered them, and then withdrew the sword of the one who was fastest asleep. Then she cut the bonds of Aristomenes

s: Aristomenes is wounded by Lacedæmonians (during an attack by both Lacedæmonian kings)
q: And Aristomenes with his picked men made a sally when the night was considerably advanced, and stole a march upon the enemy by getting to Amyclæ before daybreak, and seized the fort and plundered Amyclæ, and was off again before help could come from Sparta. And he afterwards overran the whole country, till making an attack on more than half the Lacedæmonian army under both their kings, he received several wounds as he defended himself valiantly

s: Theoclus the seer is a Messenian seer (descendant of Eumantis)
q: and the Messenian seer being Theoclus, a descendant of Eumantis

s: Theoclus the seer descends from Eumantis
q: and the Messenian seer being Theoclus, a descendant of Eumantis (a native of Elis and one of the Iamidæ whom Cresphontes had introduced into Messene)

s: Messenians calls back all the Messenians (except those fighting with remarkable bravery)
q: And Aristomenes called all the Messenians back from the fight, except those who were fighting with remarkable bravery

s: Eira is captured by Lacedæmonians
q: Eira was taken, and the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians finished

s: the capture of Eira ends the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians
q: Eira was taken, and the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians finished

s: the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians ends in the capture of Eira
q: Eira was taken, and the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians finished

s: Arcadians welcomes Messenians (at Mount Lycæus)
q: And when they got safe to Mount Lycæus the Arcadians welcomed them, and treated them kindly in other respects, and invited them to dwell in their cities, and said they would give them a share of the land.

s: Emperamus and the Spartans is a Spartan force
q: What the herdsman said seemed trustworthy, and he led Emperamus and the Spartan force.

s: Arcadians offers land to Messenians (in their cities)
q: And when they got safe to Mount Lycæus the Arcadians welcomed them, and treated them kindly in other respects, and invited them to dwell in their cities, and said they would give them a share of the land.

s: Aristocrates discloses the design of Aristomenes (by letter to Anaxander at Sparta)
q: For Aristocrates had at once disclosed by letter the design of Aristomenes, and given the letter to his most trusty slave, and sent it to Anaxander at Sparta.

s: Aristocrates is stoned by Arcadians (after his treason was exposed)
q: So the Arcadians stoned Aristocrates to death, and cast him unburied out of their borders

s: Mount Lycæus is a place of refuge (for the surviving Messenians)
q: And when they got safe to Mount Lycæus the Arcadians welcomed them

s: Cyllene is a arsenal of Elis
q: to Cyllene the arsenal of Elis.

s: Aristomenes is a Messenian leader
q: The first who noticed that the enemy had got inside the walls, and who rushed up to the fray, were Gorgus the son of Aristomenes, and Aristomenes himself, and Theoclus the seer and Manticlus his son

s: Elis supplies the Messenian colony (during its winter at Cyllene)
q: the people of Elis provided them with supplies and money

s: the Messenian colony is renamed Messene (from Zancle)
q: But the name of the town they changed from Zancle to Messene.

s: Anaxilas is king of Rhegium
q: Meantime Anaxilas sent a message to the Messenians inviting them to Italy. He was King at Rhegium

s: Anaxilas is descended from Alcidamidas (fourth in descent)
q: He was King at Rhegium, and fourth in descent from Alcidamidas, who had migrated from Messene to Rhegium

s: Rhegium is ruled by Anaxilas
q: Meantime Anaxilas sent a message to the Messenians inviting them to Italy. He was King at Rhegium

s: Zancle is in Sicily (in a fertile country)
q: the people of Zancle were at variance with him, and that they had a fertile country and a city in the rich part of Sicily

s: the people of Zancle is conquered by Anaxilas (with the Messenians’ assistance)
q: But now Anaxilas conquered the people of Zancle who put out to sea in their fleet, and the Messenians conquered them on land.

s: the people of Zancle becomes one people with the Messenian colony (after mutual pledges)
q: And after that they took the people of Zancle from the altars, and having mutually given and received pledges dwelt together as one people.

s: Zancle is renamed Messene (after the Messenian conquest)
q: But the name of the town they changed from Zancle to Messene.

s: Aristomenes is parent of Gorgus the son of Aristomenes (father)
q: The first who noticed that the enemy had got inside the walls, and who rushed up to the fray, were Gorgus the son of Aristomenes, and Aristomenes himself

s: Perieres is a leader of Zancle (from Chalcis)
q: their leaders were Cratæmenes the Samian and Perieres from Chalcis.

s: Manticlus builds the temple of Hercules (for the new colony)
q: And Manticlus built a temple of Hercules for the new colony

s: the temple of Hercules is dedicated to Hercules
q: And Manticlus built a temple of Hercules for the new colony

s: the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians occurs in the 28th Olympiad (first year)
q: Eira was taken, and the second war between the Lacedæmonians and the Messenians finished, in the Archonship over the Athenians of Autosthenes, in the first year of the 28th Olympiad

s: Miltiades is archon of Athens (during the 29th Olympiad)
q: All this took place in the 29th Olympiad, in which Chionis the Laconian was victor the second time, and Miltiades was Archon at Athens.

s: Aristomenes is sibling of Agnagora (brother)
q: Euergetidas a man held in especial honour at Messene, who had improved his fortunes by his marriage with Agnagora, the sister of Aristomenes.

s: Theoclus the seer is a seer (Messenian religious figure)
q: The first who noticed that the enemy had got inside the walls, and who rushed up to the fray, were Gorgus the son of Aristomenes, and Aristomenes himself, and Theoclus the seer and Manticlus his son

s: Manticlus is a Messenian leader
q: To the command of this portion of the army he appointed Gorgus and Manticlus

s: Theoclus the seer is parent of Manticlus (father)
q: The first who noticed that the enemy had got inside the walls, and who rushed up to the fray, were Gorgus the son of Aristomenes, and Aristomenes himself, and Theoclus the seer and Manticlus his son

s: Aristomenes refuses the leadership (of those going on the new colony)
q: Meantime Aristomenes, when he refused the leadership of those who were going on the new colony

s: Lacedæmonians conquer Messenia (after Aristomenes's death)
q: And the Lacedæmonians, when they had made themselves masters of Messenia

s: Lacedæmonians divide Messenia (among themselves, excepting Asinæi territory)
q: shared it out among themselves all but the territory of the Asinæi

s: Lacedæmonians grant Mothone (to the people of Nauplia)
q: and Mothone they gave to the people of Nauplia who had recently been ejected by the Argives.

s: Messenians are incorporated as Helots (after capture at Eira)
q: And the Messenians who were captured at Eira, and compulsorily incorporated among the Helots

s: Messenians revolt against Lacedæmonians (in the Second Messenian revolt)
q: revolted again from the Lacedæmonians in the 79th Olympiad

s: Poseidon punishes those Spartans (for violating his rights of sanctuary)
q: And the wrath of Poseidon came upon those Spartans who had violated his rights of sanctuary

s: Helots revolt from Lacedæmonians (the Helots who were Messenians)
q: And it was after this calamity that the Helots who were Messenians revolted and went to Mount Ithome.

s: Athenians dismiss Athenian troops (from Ithome because the Lacedæmonians suspected them of revolutionary ideas)
q: But when these Athenian troops came they suspected them as likely to introduce revolutionary ideas among their own men, so in their suspicion they soon sent them home again from Ithome.

s: Aristomenes marries sister to Tharyx of Phigalia (his sister Agnagora)
q: married his sister Agnagora to Tharyx of Phigalia

s: Athenians become friendly to Argives (after the Lacedæmonians dismissed their troops)
q: But when the Athenians observed that suspicion on the part of the Lacedæmonians they were indignant and became friendly to the Argives

s: Athenians give Naupactus (to the Messenians after taking it from the Locrians)
q: gave Naupactus to them, (having taken it from the Locrians in Ætolia called Ozolæ).

s: Messenians occupy Naupactus (after surrendering at Ithome)
q: when those of the Messenians who were besieged at Ithome were allowed to surrender upon conditions, gave Naupactus to them

s: Messenians marches against Œniadæ
q: And as they knew that the Œniadæ, who had a rich soil in Acarnania, had been for all time at variance with the Athenians, they marched against them.

s: Messenians escape to Naupactus (after breaking through the Acarnanian blockade of Œniadæ)
q: and by the assistance of the Ætolians who were friendly to them got safe to Naupactus.

s: Messenians use as base Naupactus (against the Peloponnese)
q: For they made Naupactus a base against the Peloponnese

s: Messenians assist Athenians (with bowmen from Naupactus at Sphacteria)
q: when the Spartans were cut off at Sphacteria some Messenian bowmen from Naupactus assisted the Athenians.

s: Lacedæmonians drive out Messenians (from Naupactus after the Athenian defeat at Ægos-potamoi)
q: the Lacedæmonians being masters of the sea drove the Messenians from Naupactus

s: Messenians settle in Euesperitæ (most of the exiles went to Libya)
q: but most to Libya to the Euesperitæ

s: Aristomenes marries daughter to Damothoidas of Lepreum (his eldest daughter)
q: and his two eldest daughters to Damothoidas of Lepreum and Theopompus of Heræum

s: Comon leads Messenians (at Sphacteria and during their settlement among the Euesperitæ)
q: To them went most of the Messenians under Comon, who had been their General at Sphacteria.

s: Thebans recall Messenians (from their wanderings to the Peloponnese after Leuctra)
q: And now the Thebans after the victory of Leuctra sent messengers to Italy and Sicily and to the Euesperitæ, to recall the Messenians from their wanderings to the Peloponnese.

s: Epaminondas restores Messenians (their country and cities)
q: But do you in return restore to the Messenians their country and cities

s: Epiteles is a Argive general (son of Æschines and restorer of Messene)
q: who revealed the dream to Epiteles the son of Æschines, whom the Argives chose as their General and the restorer of Messene.

s: Castor and Pollux oppose Messenians (before the battle at Stenyclerus; later appeased)
q: The wrath of Castor and Pollux against the Messenians began before the battle at Stenyclerus

s: Aristomenes marries daughter to Theopompus of Heræum (his second eldest daughter)
q: and his two eldest daughters to Damothoidas of Lepreum and Theopompus of Heræum

s: Epaminondas builds Messene (city) (as a base against the Lacedæmonians)
q: And they called the capital Messene, and they restored others of their towns.

s: Messene (city) is called Messene (as the capital)
q: And they called the capital Messene

s: Messenians return to Peloponnese (287 years after the capture of Eira)
q: Thus the Messenians returned to the Peloponnese, and were restored to their country, 287 years after the capture of Eira

s: Messenians preserve Doric dialect (after nearly 300 years of exile)
q: nor did they change their Doric dialect, but even to our day they preserve it purer than any other of the Peloponnesians.

s: Lacedæmonians oppose Messenians (after the Phocian War withdrew the Thebans from the Peloponnese)
q: then the Lacedæmonians pricked up their courage, and could no longer keep their hands off the Messenians.

s: Messenians receive aid from Macedonians (under Philip, son of Amyntas)
q: And eventually the Messenians got the help of Philip, the son of Amyntas, and the Macedonians

s: Messenians occupy Elis (by cunning and audacity)
q: And not long afterwards the Messenians occupied Elis, partly by cunning partly by audacity.

s: Elis is a Peloponnesian people (formerly regarded as the most orderly)
q: The people of Elis in ancient times were the most orderly of all the Peloponnesians

s: Messenians control Elis (after expelling the Lacedæmonian party)
q: But when the Messenians got in, in the way I have described, they expelled from the town the Lacedæmonian party, and entrusted the town to their own friends.

s: Aristomenes has daughter unnamed third daughter (a third daughter)
q: And Aristomenes had a third daughter

s: Aristomenes is considered noblest Greek of his time (by Damagetus)
q: and he married her, thinking her father far the noblest Greek of his time.

s: Aristomenes consults oracle (at Delphi)
q: And he himself went to Delphi and consulted the oracle.

s: Aristomenes dies at Rhodes (from illness before traveling to Sardis and Ecbatana)
q: And Aristomenes went to Rhodes with his daughter, and from thence he intended to go to Sardis to Ardys the son of Gyges, and to Ecbatana the royal residence of the Medes to the Court of King Phraortes, but before he could carry out this intention he chanced to die of some illness

s: Aristomenes receives monument from Damagetus (after his death)
q: And Damagetus and the people of Rhodes built a splendid monument to him, and paid honours to his memory.

s: capture of Messene involved Demetrius, son of Philip (Macedonian attack)
q: And no long time after this action at Elis the Macedonians under Demetrius, the son of Philip the son of Demetrius, attacked Messene.

s: Messene has circular wall (entirely constructed of stone)
q: And round Messene is a circular wall entirely constructed of stone, and towers and battlements are built on it.

s: Messene has towers and battlements (built on its circular wall)
q: And round Messene is a circular wall entirely constructed of stone, and towers and battlements are built on it.

s: Messenians joined Achæan league (in process of time)
q: In process of time however the Messenians joined the Achæan League.

s: Messenians received Arcadians (after the capture of Megalopolis)
q: Philopœmen the son of Craugis and those who escaped with him (and they say that rather more than two thirds of the people of Megalopolis got away) were kindly received by the Messenians

s: Messenians assigned equal rights to Arcadians
q: The Messenians even went so far as to assign to the Arcadians equal rights to themselves.

s: Messenians joined Aratus (with the Achæans at Sellasia)
q: For when they fought against Cleomenes at Sellasia they joined Aratus and the Achæans in taking Sparta.

s: Messenians captured Philopœmen, son of Craugis (after defeating his cavalry)
q: the Messenians having the advantage of ground beat them in battle, and took Philopœmen alive.

s: Messenians rejoined Achæan league (after the punishment of those guilty of Philopœmen’s death)
q: those Messenians who were guilty of the death of Philopœmen were punished, and Messene again joined the Achæan League.

s: Achæan league was hostile to Lacedæmonians (openly)
q: as the Achæans were most openly hostile to the Lacedæmonians.

s: Achæans ravaged Messenia (after a difference with the Messenians)
q: And the Achæans after this, in consequence of some difference with the Messenians, marched out against them in full force, and ravaged their territory.

s: Demetrius, son of Philip is a Macedonian commander
q: And no long time after this action at Elis the Macedonians under Demetrius, the son of Philip the son of Demetrius, attacked Messene.

s: Cleomenes is son of Leonidas
q: Cleomenes, the son of Leonidas and grandson of Cleonymus

s: Cleomenes captured Megalopolis (in truce time)
q: And not long afterwards Cleomenes, the son of Leonidas and grandson of Cleonymus, took Megalopolis the chief town of the Arcadians in truce time.

s: Megalopolis is a chief town of the Arcadians
q: took Megalopolis the chief town of the Arcadians in truce time

s: Philopœmen, son of Craugis is son of Craugis
q: Philopœmen the son of Craugis

s: Philopœmen, son of Craugis was received by Messenians (with the Megalopolitans who escaped)
q: Philopœmen the son of Craugis and those who escaped with him (and they say that rather more than two thirds of the people of Megalopolis got away) were kindly received by the Messenians

s: Dinocrates was elected ruler of the Messenians (recently elected)
q: but Dinocrates a prominent man among the people, who had been recently elected ruler of the Messenians

s: Dinocrates protected Messenians (by occupying the byroads between Messenia and Arcadia)
q: having occupied the byroads between Messenia and Arcadia he protected[58] the Messenians in their town and in all the neighbouring districts

s: Abia is a town by the sea (in Messenia)
q: There is in our days in Messenia, about 20 stades from the Chœrian dell, a town by the sea called Abia.

s: Abia was called Ire (in old times)
q: They say in old times it was called Ire

s: Demetrius, son of Philip is son of Philip
q: the Macedonians under Demetrius, the son of Philip the son of Demetrius

s: Pharæ is distant from Abia (about 80 stades)
q: And Pharæ is distant from Abia about 80 stades

s: Augustus assigned Pharæ (to Laconia)
q: The Emperor Augustus ordered the Messenians at Pharæ to be ranked under Laconia.

s: Thuria was called Anthea (by Homer)
q: Thuria,--which they say Homer called Anthea in his verses.

s: Augustus gave Thuria (to the Spartans)
q: And Augustus gave Thuria to the Spartans.

s: Thuria has Aris (a river flowing by the town in the plain)
q: And a river called Aris flows by their town in the plain.

s: Clepsydra supplies Zeus (water taken daily to his temple)
q: and every day they take water from this spring to the temple of Zeus of Ithome.

s: Zeus was reared by Ithome (according to the Messenian tradition)
q: They say that Zeus was reared among them, and that Ithome and Neda were his nurses

s: Zeus has statue by Ageladas (Zeus of Ithome)
q: And the statue of Zeus is the work of Ageladas

s: Carnasian grove is a grove (mostly of cypress trees; formerly called Œchalia)
q: what was called of old Œchalia, but in our day the Carnasian grove, mostly of cypress trees.

s: Demetrius, son of Philip led Macedonian army (against Messene)
q: And Demetrius chanced to put in at one of the least frequented harbours of Argolis: and without losing time he led his army by the shortest cuts through the country to Messene.

s: Carnasian grove contains Messenian Mysteries (Mysteries of the Great Goddesses)
q: the rites of the Great Goddesses, who have their Mysteries at the Carnasian grove

s: Messenian Mysteries rank second only to Eleusinian Mysteries (in sanctity, in Pausanias’ opinion)
q: but they are in my opinion second only in sanctity to the Eleusinian Mysteries.

s: Aristomenes has tomb at Messene (claimed to contain his remains)
q: There is here also the tomb of Aristomenes, and not a mere cenotaph, if their account is correct.

s: Aristomenes supported Thebans (at the battle of Leuctra according to the Messenians)
q: they amuse themselves with the fancy that Aristomenes though no longer alive was present at the fight at Leuctra, and they say he fought for the Thebans

s: battle of Leuctra was won by Thebans (with Aristomenes’ shield displayed as a trophy)
q: And after the Thebans won their victory, they offered Aristomenes’ shield again to Trophonius as a votive offering.

s: Epaminondas is statue at Messene (in the temple of Æsculapius)
q: there are statues of Thebes and Epaminondas the son of Cleommis

s: Messene has temple of Serapis and Isis (not far from the theatre)
q: And not far from the theatre is the temple of Serapis and Isis.

s: restoration of Messene includes Messenian restoration (return to the ancestral country after dispersion)
q: the Deity, having scattered them to the ends of the earth, and to places most remote from the Peloponnese, restored them to their own country a long time afterwards.

s: Macedonians attacked Messene (under Demetrius, son of Philip)
q: the Macedonians under Demetrius, the son of Philip the son of Demetrius, attacked Messene.

s: Macedonians were defeated by Messenians (at Messene)
q: The Macedonians from their courage and tactical skill fought at first like lions: but at last spent with their long march, and not only pressed hard by men, but pelted with tiles and stones by the women, fled in disorder.

s: Messene is situated under Ithome (the city of the Messenians)
q: you come to the city of the Messenians under Mount Ithome

s: Pamisus flows through arable land (clear and limpid; navigable some 10 stades inland)
q: the Pamisus flows clear and limpid through arable land, and is navigable some 10 stades inland.

s: Corone is a town (near the sea)
q: On the right of the Pamisus is Corone, a town near the sea, and under the mountain Mathia.

s: Corone lies under Mathia
q: On the right of the Pamisus is Corone, a town near the sea, and under the mountain Mathia.

s: Corone was called Æpea (formerly)
q: The name of the town was of old Æpea

s: Corone was renamed after Coronea (after the restoration of the Messenians)
q: but after the Messenians were restored to the Peloponnese by the Thebans, they say that Epimelides, who was sent to rebuild it, called it Coronea

s: Corone has temple of Artemis (called the Rearer of children)
q: The gods here who have temples are Artemis called the Rearer of children, and Dionysus, and Æsculapius.

s: Corone has temple of Dionysus
q: The gods here who have temples are Artemis called the Rearer of children, and Dionysus, and Æsculapius.

s: Corone has temple of Æsculapius
q: The gods here who have temples are Artemis called the Rearer of children, and Dionysus, and Æsculapius.

s: Pamisus is about 80 stades from Messene
q: From Messene to the mouth of the Pamisus is about 80 stades

s: Corone has statue of Zeus Soter (brazen statue in the market-place)
q: there is a brazen statue of Zeus Soter in the market-place.

s: Corone has statue of Athene (brazen statue in the citadel, holding a crow)
q: There is also a brazen statue of Athene in the citadel in the open air, with a crow in her hand.

s: Apollo is worshipped as Corydus (at a temple near the sea)
q: They call the god Corydus.

s: Apollo heals diseases (according to the Messenian tradition)
q: the god heals diseases. They call the god Corydus.

s: Corydus has statue of Apollo (wooden statue)
q: His statue here is of wood

s: Argonauts dedicate Apollo (a brazen statue made by Argeotas)
q: but there is a brazen statue the work of Argeotas, a votive offering they say of the Argonauts.

s: Colonides has inhabitants Dryopes (they say they were not Messenians)
q: Its inhabitants say they were not Messenians but were brought by Colænus from Attica

s: Asine is a town (by the sea in Messenia)
q: And Asine lies by the sea just as the old Asine in Argolis did

s: Asine is inhabited by Dryopes (its inhabitants retain and celebrate the name)
q: And the Asinæi are the only descendants of the Dryopes that still plume themselves on that name

s: Pamisus receives sea fish (especially in spring)
q: And some sea fish swim up it especially at the season of spring

s: Asine has temple of Dryops (with an ancient statue and annual mysteries)
q: but a temple and ancient statue of Dryops, whose mysteries they celebrate annually

s: Hercules defeats Dryopes (when Phylas was king)
q: in the third generation afterwards, when Phylas was king, the Dryopes were beaten in battle by Hercules

s: Dryopes are offered to Apollo (after their defeat by Hercules)
q: and were taken to Delphi and offered to Apollo.

s: Mothone was called Pedasus (before and after the Trojan War)
q: Mothone, which before the expedition against Troy and even subsequently to that war was called Pedasus

s: Mothone is named after Mothon (according to the narrator’s opinion)
q: But in my opinion the Rock called Mothon gave its name to Mothone

s: Mothone has natural harbour Mothon (the rock narrows the entrance and breaks the waves)
q: for being much of it sunken under the water it narrows the entrance for ships, and at the same time is a kind of breakwater against the violence of the waves.

s: Lacedæmonians give Mothone (to the people of Nauplia)
q: the Lacedæmonians, in the days when Damocratidas was king at Argos, gave Mothone to the people of Nauplia

s: Mothone is inhabited by Nauplia (after the Nauplians were expelled from their city)
q: gave Mothone to the people of Nauplia, who had been expelled from their city for their Laconian proclivities

s: Trajan grants Mothone (a free constitution)
q: And the Emperor Trajan granted the people of Mothone a free constitution.

s: Mothone's capture by the Illyrians is a piratic attack (the town was partly depopulated)
q: Then the Illyrians in the height of their daring captured many men and still more women, and clapped them on board, and sailed away for the Ionian sea, having half stripped the town of its population.

s: Illyrians sails to Mothone (with friendly intent after making piratic excursions)
q: And the Illyrians, when they had once tasted the sweets of conquest, longed for more and still more, and equipped a fleet, and made piratic excursions everywhere, and sailed to Mothone and anchored there as with friendly intent

s: Mothone has temple of Artemis
q: There is also a temple of Artemis here

s: Coryphasium is a promontory (near Pylos)
q: From Mothone to the promontory of Coryphasium is about 100 stades

s: Pylos was founded by Pylos (founder) (the founder brought Leleges from Megaris)
q: near it is Pylos, which was founded by Pylos, the son of Cleson, who brought from Megaris the Leleges who then occupied Megaris.

s: Pylos is associated with Neleus (Homer calls it the city of Neleus)
q: king Neleus advanced Pylos to such renown that Homer in his Iliad calls it the city of Neleus.

s: Pylos has temple of Athene (called Coryphasia)
q: There is a temple there of Athene called Coryphasia

s: Pylos has house of Nestor's house (with a painting of Nestor)
q: and a house called Nestor’s house, in which is a painting of Nestor

s: Nestor has tomb at Pylos (inside the city)
q: and there is his tomb inside the city

s: Pylos has cave of Nestor (the cave was said to be his ox-stall)
q: there is a cave inside the city, which they say was the stall of the oxen of Nestor and still earlier of Neleus.

s: Sphacteria is a island (before the harbour of Pylos)
q: Before the harbour is the island Sphacteria

s: Sphacteria is famous for Lacedæmonians (their reverses there made it world-famous)
q: So too the reverses of the Lacedæmonians at Sphacteria made the place world-famed.

s: Athenians erect Victory (a brazen statue in the Acropolis commemorating Sphacteria)
q: And the Athenians erected a brazen statue of Victory in their Acropolis as a record of their success at Sphacteria.

s: Dionysus’ spring is caused by Dionysus (according to local tradition)
q: They say the water welled up in consequence of Dionysus striking the ground with his thyrsus, and so they call the spring Dionysus’ spring.

s: Peloponnese is divided into Arcadia (one of five divisions)
q: Those Greeks, who say that the Peloponnese is divided into five parts and no more, are obliged to admit that the people of Elis as well as the Arcadians dwell in the division of the Arcadians

s: Dryopes come from Mount Parnassus (immigration into the Peloponnese)
q: And the Dryopes came into the Peloponnese from Mount Parnassus

s: Dorians come from Mount Œta (immigration into the Peloponnese)
q: the Dorians from Mount Œta.

s: Elis originates in Calydon (and other parts of Ætolia)
q: We know that the people of Elis originally came from Calydon and other parts of Ætolia.

s: Aethlius is son of Zeus (by Protogenea)
q: The first king in this land was they say Aethlius, the son of Zeus by Protogenea the daughter of Deucalion

s: Endymion has son Epeus
q: and had three sons, Pæon and Epeus and Ætolus, and one daughter Eurycyde.

s: Endymion is father of Ætolus (with Asterodia or another named wife)
q: and had three sons, Pæon and Epeus and Ætolus, and one daughter Eurycyde.

s: Peloponnese is divided into Achaia (one of five divisions)
q: Those Greeks, who say that the Peloponnese is divided into five parts and no more, are obliged to admit that the people of Elis as well as the Arcadians dwell in the division of the Arcadians, and that the second division is Achaia

s: Pelops is a Lydian (originating in Asia Minor)
q: Pelops the Lydian, who had crossed over from Asia Minor.

s: Pelops occupies Olympia (after deposing Œnomaus)
q: And after his death Pelops occupied Pisæa and Olympia

s: Pelops builds temple to Hermes (first in the Peloponnese)
q: Pelops (so the people of Elis say) was the first in the Peloponnese to build a temple to Hermes and sacrifice to him

s: Ætolus rules Elis (after Epeus)
q: And Ætolus, the king after Epeus, had to flee from the Peloponnese

s: Ætolus gives name to Ætolia (after fleeing to the Achelous region)
q: So Ætolus the son of Endymion fled to the mainland, to the neighbourhood of the river Achelous, which was called Ætolia after him.

s: Eleus reigns over the kingdom of the Epeans
q: And the kingdom of the Epeans was reigned over by Eleus

s: Eleus is son of Eurycyde (and traditionally of Poseidon)
q: And the kingdom of the Epeans was reigned over by Eleus, the son of Eurycyde, the daughter of Endymion and (if we may believe the tradition) Poseidon.

s: Arcadians inhabit Arcadia (indigenous population)
q: The indigenous races that inhabit the Peloponnese are Arcadians and Achæans.

s: Eleans are renamed from Epeans (under Eleus)
q: And the people in his dominions now changed their names from Epeans to Eleans.

s: Augeas is son of Eleus (king of Elis)
q: And Eleus had a son called Augeas.

s: Augeas rules Elis (with Amarynceus and the sons of Actor sharing administration)
q: And to Amarynceus Augeas gave a share of his power at Elis; and Actor and his sons also, who were natives of Elis, shared in the administration of the kingdom.

s: Augeas owns oxen and goats (in exceptionally large numbers)
q: The oxen and goats of this Augeas were so numerous that most of the country could not be cultivated for their dung.

s: Hercules clears Elis (by diverting the Menius)
q: Hercules therefore, whether for a part of Elis or some other reward, was persuaded by him to clear the country of this dung. And he effected this by turning the river Menius on to it.

s: Phyleus receives Elis (from Hercules after the conquest)
q: And to Phyleus Hercules gave up Elis and other places

s: Hercules captures Elis (with Argive, Theban, and Arcadian forces)
q: Hercules afterwards captured and sacked Elis, having got together an army of Argives Thebans and Arcadians

s: Hercules is assisted by Argives (in the campaign against Elis)
q: Hercules afterwards captured and sacked Elis, having got together an army of Argives Thebans and Arcadians

s: Pylos assists Elis (against Hercules)
q: and the people of Elis were assisted by the men of Pylos in Elis and by the men of Pisa.

s: Achæans inhabit Peloponnese (indigenous population)
q: The indigenous races that inhabit the Peloponnese are Arcadians and Achæans.

s: Pisa assists Elis (against Hercules)
q: and the people of Elis were assisted by the men of Pylos in Elis and by the men of Pisa.

s: Elis does not participate in Isthmian games (because of the curse associated with the sons of Molione)
q: And these curses of Moline are observed up to this day, and all the athletes at Elis make a practice of never going to the Isthmian contest.

s: Iphitus revives Olympian games (with the cooperation of Elis)
q: Iphitus, who was of the same family as Oxylus, and a contemporary of Lycurgus the Lacedæmonian legislator, revived the contest at Olympia, and renewed the public gathering there

s: Iphitus establishes Olympic truce (for the duration of the games)
q: and established a truce as long as the games lasted.

s: Elis sacrifices to Hercules (after Iphitus persuaded the Eleans)
q: Iphitus also persuaded the people of Elis to sacrifice to Hercules, for before this they had an idea that Hercules was hostile to them.

s: Elis participates in Trojan war
q: The people of Elis took part in the Trojan war

s: Elis participates in Persian invasion of Greece (against the invading Persians)
q: and also in the battles against the Persians when they invaded Greece.

s: Elis allies with Lacedæmonians (reluctantly in the invasion of Attica)
q: they joined the Lacedæmonians not without reluctance in invading Attica

s: Elis fights against Lacedæmonians (after forming an alliance with Mantineans and Athenians)
q: not long after they fought against the Lacedæmonians, having formed an alliance with the Mantineans the Argives and the Athenians.

s: Elis joins Macedonians (under Philip, amid internal factions)
q: the people of Elis, worn out with intestine factions, joined the Macedonians, but not to the point of fighting against the Greeks at Chæronea.

s: Achæans are driven from Achaia (by the Dorians)
q: And the Achæans were driven out of their own land by the Dorians

s: Elis participates in Philip (attack on the Lacedæmonians)
q: But they participated in the attack of Philip upon the Lacedæmonians by reason of their ancient hatred to them.

s: Elis fights against Macedonians (after Alexander's death, alongside the Greeks)
q: But after the death of Alexander they joined the Greeks in fighting against Antipater and the Macedonians.

s: Dorians drives out Achæans (from their own land)
q: And the Achæans were driven out of their own land by the Dorians, but did not however evacuate the Peloponnese

s: Ionians inhabit Achaia (before the Achæan occupation)
q: but did not however evacuate the Peloponnese, but dispossessed the Ionians that lived in what was then called Ægialus, but is now called after them Achaia.

s: Arcadians remain in Arcadia (continuously to the present)
q: The Arcadians on the other hand have always up to this day remained in Arcadia.

s: Corinthians are introduced into Peloponnese (by the Roman Emperor)
q: The latest importation were the present Corinthians, who were introduced into the Peloponnese some 217 years ago by the Roman Emperor.

s: Elis possesses flax of Elis (a local wonder)
q: Among the wonders of Elis are the flax, which grows here alone and in no other part of Greece

s: Elis contains Samicum (a place by the sea)
q: And as you go from the district of Elis there is a place by the sea called Samicum

s: Triphylia contains Lepreus
q: and beyond it on the right is the district called Triphylia, and the city Lepreus in it.

s: Lepreus has victors recognized by men of Elis (at Olympia)
q: For the victors at Olympia that came from Lepreus were pronounced by the herald men of Elis.

s: Lepreus is founded by Pyrgeus (according to one tradition)
q: The city got its name they say from Lepreus the son of Pyrgeus its founder.

s: Lepreus has spring Arene (spring near Lepreus) (near the city)
q: And not far from the city Lepreus is a spring called Arene: it got this name according to tradition from the wife of Aphareus.

s: Aniger is a river (flowing to the sea at Samicum)
q: And as you return to Samicum, and go through it, the river Aniger has its outlet to the sea.

s: Aniger rises in Lapithus (an Arcadian mountain)
q: This river Aniger rises in the Arcadian mountain Lapithus

s: Aniger receives tributary Acidas
q: Before receiving its tributary the Acidas

s: Nymphs of the Aniger have cave Aniger (the cave is named for them)
q: There is at Samicum a cave, not far from the river, called the cave of the Nymphs of the Aniger.

s: Arene (ancient city) is identified with Samicum (as the ancient name of Samicum)
q: The most credible account seems to me that of those who think that the ancient name of Samicum earlier than the time of the heroes was Arene.

s: Scillus is a town of Triphylia
q: Scillus was one of the towns of Triphylia

s: Scillus is allied with Pisa (during the war against Elis)
q: in the war between the people of Elis and Pisa the people of Scillus openly allied themselves to the people of Pisa

s: Lacedæmonians give Scillus (to Xenophon)
q: But the Lacedæmonians afterwards sliced Scillus from Elis, and gave it to Xenophon (the son of Gryllus)

s: Xenophon is son of Gryllus
q: gave it to Xenophon (the son of Gryllus)

s: Xenophon builds Artemis (a temple and grove at Scillus)
q: he lived at Scillus and built a temple and grove to Ephesian Artemis.

s: Selinus flows through Scillus (the district)
q: And the river Selinus flows through the district.
